beats.say: And the whole model is about three hundred megabytes, or eighty when quantized.
Inside, every request takes the same path. Text is first turned into phonemes, the sounds of the words.
Each phoneme is mapped to a number the model understands.
The model turns those numbers into audio, at twenty four thousand samples a second.

chapters.title: From text to tokens
chapters.say: How does a sentence become something a neural network can read?

beats.say: This method does the first step. It hands the text to a phonemizer, keeping punctuation and stress marks.
A lock wraps the call, so only one thread uses the phonemizer at a time.
Then anything outside the model's vocabulary is filtered out.
Tokenizing is a lookup. Each phoneme is replaced by its id in the vocabulary.
But first comes a hard limit. Give it more phonemes than the limit, and it refuses.

chapters.title: Cutting long text
chapters.say: The model reads at most five hundred and ten phonemes at once. So what happens to a long paragraph?

scenes.heading: Where it is allowed to cut

beats.say: Long input is split into batches, and the code looks for the least disruptive place to cut.
The first choice is the end of a sentence.
The second is a clause break, like a comma.
And the third is any gap between words.
Filling every batch to the limit would leave a short one at the end, and a short batch is spoken at a different rate and loudness.
So it first counts the fewest batches it can get away with.
Then a binary search finds the smallest batch size that still needs no more batches than that.
The result is batches of nearly equal length.
Each batch holds at most five hundred and ten phonemes, and the audio comes out at twenty four thousand samples a second.
Trimming removes the silence at the end of a batch, so a pause is added back: a quarter second after a sentence, a tenth after a clause.

chapters.title: One pass through the model
chapters.say: Finally, the part that actually makes sound.

beats.say: The model takes three inputs. First the tokens, padded with a zero on each side.
Second, a style vector taken from the chosen voice.
And third, the speed.
One call runs the network, and the first output is the audio.
When the model provides them, a second output carries durations, which the library uses to work out where each phoneme starts.
Text, phonemes, tokens, one model call, and you have speech.
